deasy_request: Tambahan: Siapa yang impor lebih banyak (EGs) environment goods list (termasuk solar panel, dll)
answer: Not available in this dataset. Each firm reports only one yearly total for the imported raw materials it used, with no list of what was bought, so solar panels and other environmental goods cannot be picked out.
what_is_missing: a record of what each firm imported, item by item (customs product codes, e.g. the 6-digit HS code used worldwide to identify goods such as solar panels), with the amount paid, for each year
what_exists_instead: one yearly total per firm of imported raw materials used (import_value_nominal; import_flag = 1 when above zero; r_ln_import_nominal = its log), with no product, country or date detail
why_total_cannot_stand_in: the total mixes every imported item and cannot be split by product; the survey field map (downstream/contracts/variable_year_evidence.csv, checked against the 2010-2015 questionnaire layouts; later years use the same field code) names the source field RIMVCU = imported raw material used, so imported machines and equipment such as solar panels are probably not in it at all
what_would_be_needed: (1) customs import records for each firm, item by item (product code, amount paid, date), that can be linked to the firms in this survey; (2) an agreed list of environmental goods with their product codes, e.g. the APEC list of 54 products (APEC = Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation); (3) a table that translates product codes between versions (HS = the world customs code list, BTKI = Indonesia's version), because the codes change every few years
related_exhibits_not_an_answer: NOT an answer to this question: R1 file 01_group_shares_support (share of firms importing each year) and R3 files 02 and 04 (do importers cut energy and CO2 more often?) use this same total only to mark importers of any raw material; they say nothing about environmental goods. The importer share jumps partway through the period, likely a change in how imports were recorded (see R1 file 01).
